subject: psychology
title: Psychopathology: OCD & Biological Approach
welcome_lead: Twin studies and serotonin — OCD has a strongly biological signature.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology OCD biological explanation: genetic, neural, SSRI drug therapy.
final_note: OCD is the textbook case for biological explanation and pharmacological treatment.

concepts.def: Repetitive behaviour performed to reduce anxiety.
Gene linked to disorder, e.g. SERT (serotonin transporter).
Genetic vulnerability triggered by environmental stress.
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor — first-line OCD drug.

walkthroughs.body_html: Nestadt et al. (2010) reviewed twin studies and concluded 68% of OCD variance in identical twins is genetic vs about 31% in fraternal twins. Lewis (1936) found 37% of OCD patients had parents with OCD. OCD is polygenic; Taylor (2013) linked up to 230 different genes.

Low serotonin levels are implicated — SSRIs that raise serotonin reduce OCD symptoms. Structural studies show abnormal function in the orbitofrontal cortex, caudate nucleus and thalamus — the 'worry circuit' that fails to filter minor concerns.

SSRIs such as fluoxetine block reuptake of serotonin into the presynaptic neuron, raising synaptic levels. Soomro et al. (2009) reviewed 17 trials and found SSRIs more effective than placebo for 3 to 4 months. They are cheap and require little effort, but cause side effects (nausea, insomnia) in around 30% of patients.
